groups.name: The Hatters of Ong's Hat
groups.meet: A ring of folding chairs round the fire, and everyone in them wears a tin-foil hat. The dog too. "Ong's Hat is named for a hat thrown up a pine tree. We think he was the first of us. The Devil out at Leeds Point is a broadcast, friend, and foil keeps it out. Sit. We made you one."
groups.hint: Their leader taps the corkboard. Red string runs from a photo of the {creature} to a pin marked {section}. "Signal's strongest there. Wear the hat."
groups.lair: Every string on the corkboard ends at one pin: {section}. "That is where the {creature} transmits from. Nobody comes back from there with their hat on straight."
groups.allHeld: "The corkboard's all crossed out. You did that. We're going to need a bigger corkboard."

visits.first: "Rest your feet. Foil's on the house."
visits.again: "Still got your hat? Good. Keep it shiny side out."

visits.first: "Three keepers down out there. We added a layer of foil to celebrate. Two layers, for safety."
visits.again: "The signal's weaker this week. We think it's you."

visits.first: "Half the pines quiet. Someone saw you on the trail and said you walk like a person with nothing in their head but good ideas."
visits.again: "We ran out of foil and used baking trays. It's fine. It's fine."

visits.first: "Nine. The dog took his hat off today. We let him. He's earned it, and so have you."
visits.again: "Sit nearer the fire. Hats reflect the heat, you see."

visits.first: "The broadcast stopped. First quiet night in forty years. We kept your chair. It's the one with the hat on it."
visits.again: "Back home, Hatter? You're one of us now. You don't have to wear the hat. But you could."

groups.name: The Porchlight Vigil
groups.meet: A long porch, a bare bulb, and a row of rocking chairs. Everyone wears sunglasses and a felt cape cut like moth wings, day or night. "Don't look at the light. Look at the moths. They spell things. The red eyes up by Point Pleasant? That's a warning, not a threat. We're here to read it for you."
groups.hint: A woman in the end chair watches the moths circle the bulb. "They're spelling {section}. And a shape. The {creature}, I'd say. Or a lamp. No, the {creature}."
groups.lair: Every moth on the bulb lands at once, in one shape. "{section}," she says. "The {creature}. They've never all agreed before."
groups.allHeld: "The moths are just flying round in circles now. That's what moths do when there's nothing left to warn about."

visits.first: "Pull up a rocker. Sunglasses are optional. The cape is not."
visits.again: "Sit. The bulb's warm and the moths are chatty tonight."

visits.first: "Someone down the hollow turned their porch light on for you. That's how it starts."
visits.again: "The moths spelled your name today. Spelt it wrong, but it was you."

visits.first: "Half the hollows lit up now. You can see the porches from the ridge, like a string of beads."
visits.again: "There's iced tea. Mind the moth in it. He's one of ours."

visits.first: "Nine porches more than last month. We had to buy bulbs in bulk."
visits.again: "Take the good rocker. The one that doesn't squeak. Mostly doesn't."

visits.first: "Every light in the hollows is on tonight. That's for you. The moths are having the best night of their lives."
visits.again: "Your rocker's kept. Your cape's on the hook. Sit a while."

groups.name: The Backwards Lodge
groups.meet: A log lodge with the door on the back. Everyone inside walks backwards and wears a car mirror on a headband. "The hidebehind is always behind you, so we face the other way. Cox wrote it all down in 1910. We take him at his word. Mind the step. It's behind you."
groups.hint: An old logger tilts his mirror until it catches the trail. "Look there. Behind you, in the glass. That's {section}, and the {creature} is in it."
groups.lair: Every mirror in the lodge turns the same way on its own. "{section}," the logger says, not turning round. "The {creature}. It's been behind us for a hundred years."
groups.allHeld: "Nothing in the mirrors now but us. Strange. We'd got used to the company."

visits.first: "Sit on the bench. Facing the wall. You'll get used to it."
visits.again: "Welcome back. Or goodbye. We can never tell which way you're going."

visits.first: "Three keepers. One of us turned round at supper and looked at the door. First time in years."
visits.again: "Stove's lit. It's behind you."

visits.first: "Half the lodge walks forwards on Sundays now. Only on Sundays. We are not reckless."
visits.again: "We polished your mirror. You don't have to wear it."

visits.first: "We took the door off the back and hung it on the front. It looks wrong. It looks wonderful."
visits.again: "Sit facing whichever way you like. Truly. We mean it now."

visits.first: "We all turned round tonight, all at once, and there was nothing behind us. Only you, coming home."
visits.again: "Your mirror's on the peg. We look at you in it sometimes, so we know you're well."

groups.name: The Blurry Society
groups.meet: A tent full of drying photos, every one of them blurry. Everyone wears smeared goggles and carries an old film camera with the focus taped off. "The big one stays out of focus on purpose. A sharp photo is a fake, so we never take one. Look at our plaster casts if you want the truth."
groups.hint: They pull a plaster cast off the shelf and point its toes at the map. "This one walked towards {section}. The {creature}. Probably. It's a bit blurry."
groups.lair: The biggest cast on the shelf has a label in shaky pen: {section}. "The {creature}," they whisper. "Even the cast came out blurry."
groups.allHeld: "Every cast is labelled now. You cleared the forest so well we can nearly see it."

visits.first: "Sit on the crate. Don't take a photo of us. You'll ruin it."
visits.again: "Back again? You look slightly out of focus. Good sign."

visits.first: "Three keepers. Our photos this week are a touch less blurry. We are worried and delighted."
visits.again: "Coffee's on. It's blurry too. That's just the steam."

visits.first: "Half the coast cleared. One of us took the tape off her focus ring. She put it back. But she took it off."
visits.again: "Tea, or a plaster cast? We have more casts."

visits.first: "We printed one sharp photo today, of you, and pinned it up. It's the only one we've ever kept."
visits.again: "Your crate's here. We wrote your name on it. A little blurry."

visits.first: "The forest is quiet, and for the first time the photos came out clear. They're all of trees. We've never been so happy."
visits.again: "Sit. Your photo's still up, the sharp one. Nobody's allowed to touch it."

groups.name: The Frog Watch
groups.meet: A ring of people in green rubber waders up to the chest, sitting on upturned buckets with a torch in every hand. Every so often they all flash them at the water. "The Frogman stood up on a bridge once and waved a sparking wand. Everyone ran. We think it was saying hello. So we say hello back. Every night. Here, have a torch."
groups.hint: Out on the water a light blinks twice. They all go quiet. "That came back from {section}. Short, short, long. That's the {creature}, that is. It's got manners."
groups.lair: Every torch in the ring flickers at once and points the same way. "{section}," someone says. "The {creature}. It's been flashing back all week, louder every night."
groups.allHeld: "Nobody flashes back now. We still wave. It's only polite."

visits.first: "Take a bucket. Waders are spare in the crate. You'll want them, it gets damp."
visits.again: "Torch working? Give it a flash. There. Lovely."

visits.first: "Three keepers. Someone on the far shore started flashing back at us, and it was a person. We were thrilled anyway."
visits.again: "Kettle's on the camp stove. Mind your waders near it, they melt."

visits.first: "Half the shore cleared. We've learned to flash a whole sentence now. It says: thank you, the one in the waders."
visits.again: "Sit. We were just flashing about you."

visits.first: "Nine. A fishing boat flashed us good night last night. The whole lake's joining in."
visits.again: "Your bucket's kept warm. Well. Kept."

visits.first: "Every light round the lake is on tonight, all flashing hello. That's for you. Even the lighthouse is having a go."
visits.again: "Your torch is on the hook. Batteries are new. We change them every week, in case."

groups.name: The Antler Choir
groups.meet: A ring of cowboy hats round the fire, every one with a pair of little felt antlers sewn on. Each of them has a harmonica. "Jackalopes copy what they hear. Sing a good tune by a fire and one sings it back from the dark. Sing a bad one and it laughs. We have been practising for some years."
groups.hint: They stop mid-song. From far off, a voice finishes the line, a little flat. "That came from {section}. The {creature}, I'd bet my hat. Never could hold a note."
groups.lair: They start a slow one, and the whole desert sings it back from one place: {section}. "The {creature}," the leader says, hat off. "Best voice out here. Worst manners."
groups.allHeld: "Nothing sings back now but the wind. The wind's tone deaf. We miss the harmony."

visits.first: "Sit and hum along. Doesn't matter what. They like enthusiasm."
visits.again: "Back for the second verse? There's always a second verse."

visits.first: "Three keepers. We wrote you a song. It's mostly about your boots, we couldn't think what rhymes with your name."
visits.again: "Coffee's in the pot. Harmonica's on the rock if you fancy."

visits.first: "Half the mesas cleared. A coyote joined in last night. Not a jackalope. Still counts, we've decided."
visits.again: "Sit nearer. You can't harmonise from over there."

visits.first: "Nine. We sewed you some antlers. They're on the hat by the fire. You don't have to wear it. It would mean a lot."
visits.again: "Your hat's warming by the fire. Antlers forward, that's the trick."

visits.first: "The desert's quiet, so we sang your song all the way through, and the whole valley sang it back. All twelve verses. Nobody can be that lonely out here now."
visits.again: "Back home, singer? Take the middle spot. It's yours."

groups.name: The Thirteen Counters
groups.meet: A jetty over black water, and a row of people with thirteen big beads round each neck and a jar of beans in each lap. "The rougarou has to count what you leave out. It can't count past twelve, so it starts over, all night, till the sun comes up. Thirteen beans. Leave them out, sleep sound. Here's your jar."
groups.hint: An old man brings back a saucer of beans from the bank and frowns at them. "These came from out by {section}. Somebody counted them twelve times over. That'll be the {creature}."
groups.lair: Every jar on the jetty has been tipped out and counted, one by one, in a long line pointing at {section}. "The {creature}," they whisper. "It got to twelve. Again."
groups.allHeld: "Nobody's counting our beans now. We count them ourselves, at night, for the company."

visits.first: "Sit. Count your beans. All thirteen? Good. Now you're safe."
visits.again: "Back again? Count them. Go on. It's the rule."

visits.first: "Three keepers. We put out a fourteenth bean for you. It's not for anything. It's just a gift."
visits.again: "Gumbo's on. It has beans in it. Thirteen. We counted."

visits.first: "Half the bayou cleared. Some of us slept with only twelve beans out last night. Very daring."
visits.again: "Pull up a crate. The frogs are loud, but they don't count."

visits.first: "Nine. We strung you a necklace. Thirteen beads. We checked it three times. Thirty-nine. We checked it thirty-nine times."
visits.again: "Your beads are on the post. Shiny side out."

visits.first: "Twelve keepers, and the bayou's quiet. Twelve. We'll give you the thirteenth ourselves: you're one of us."
visits.again: "Sit, Counter. Your jar's full. We topped it up."

groups.name: The Howl-Back Club
groups.meet: A ring of folding stools on a ridge, everyone in fluffy earmuffs, each holding a tin cup to their mouth. "The Howler isn't scary. It's lonely. Nobody howls back. So we do. The cups help with the echo. The earmuffs help with the neighbours."
groups.hint: They all howl into their cups at once. A long, sad howl answers. "That came from {section}. The {creature}. It sounds better already, doesn't it?"
groups.lair: One howl answers every cup on the ridge, from one place: {section}. "The {creature}," says the leader, taking off her earmuffs. "It's never howled that loud. It knows somebody's coming."
groups.allHeld: "Nothing howls back now. We howl anyway, a little, to the hills. Habit."

visits.first: "Take a cup. Take a breath. Owwooo. Lovely. You're a natural."
visits.again: "Back for a howl? Earmuffs on, cup up."

visits.first: "Three keepers. The hills sound friendlier this week. Less howling, more singing."
visits.again: "Cocoa's in the flask. Sip, then howl. Not the other way round."

visits.first: "Half the hills cleared. A farmer down the valley howled back at us last night. On purpose."
visits.again: "Sit. The good stool's free. The one that doesn't fold."

visits.first: "Nine. We knitted you earmuffs. Red ones. So we can see you on the ridge."
visits.again: "Your earmuffs are on the stool. Still warm."

visits.first: "The Howler's quiet tonight. Not sad quiet. Asleep quiet. You did that. One howl for you, everyone. Owwooo."
visits.again: "Back home? Howl once, so the hills know."
